subject: Plan refit request — carve feature set and downgrade path
messages:
From: Beth Carter <beth@pulsebio.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
Cc: Raj Singh <raj@pulsebio.com>
Date: Wed, 18 Apr 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Refit request — trimming features for pilot budget

Hi Hannah,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. Our finance team is pushing us to hit a lower TCO for the pilot — we're targeting ~40% less spend than the current proposal. The core use case for Q3 is 1) low-latency summarization (customer support transcripts) and 2) embeddings for search. We can give up advanced tool-calling and the realtime reranking path for the first 3 months if that helps.

Two asks:
- Can you propose a trimmed plan that keeps throughput for short sequences but removes higher-cost features (tooling, realtime rerank)?
- What does a downgrade path look like if we need to expand again to full feature set after Q3? Any stepwise re-enable fees or credits?

I've attached our Q1 usage snapshot so you can see token mix.

Appreciate a quick sketch — Raj and I have a meeting with Finance on Monday.

Best,
Beth
Beth Carter
Head of Product, PulseBio
attachments: pulsebio_usage_report_Q1.csv
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Beth Carter <beth@pulsebio.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Raj Singh <raj@pulsebio.com>
Date: Wed, 18 Apr 2028 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Refit request — trimming features for pilot budget

Hi Beth —

Thanks for the usage file, that helps a lot. Quick notes up-front:
- We can create a \"Pilot Slim\" plan that preserves the short-sequence generation SLA and embeddings, and strips: realtime reranking, function/tool-call concurrency guarantees, and some of the long-context KV cache tier.
- Pricing approach: move from our standard per-token + addon model to a fixed monthly pilot bucket (committed tokens) plus reduced per-token overage. That gives predictable spend to satisfy Finance.
- Downgrade/upgrade path: we support staged re-enablement. Typically customers: 1) start on Pilot Slim (committed month), 2) when ready to re-enable features we do a canary roll (7–14 days) to validate QoS, and 3) pro-rate any delta for the month. We can offer a one-time re-enable credit to neutralize the first-month uplift if you commit to a 6-month pilot.

I'll have Ben put together a concise quote (numbers + quick comparison matrix) — Ben, can you take the usage file and produce: Pilot Slim (3-month commit), Pilot Slim + re-enable credit (6-month commit), and Full Stack (standard) with stepwise re-enable costs? Beth/Raj — target Monday for the Finance call, so earliest deliverable needed EOD Friday.

Hannah
Hannah Schmitt
Director, Mid-Market Sales
Redwood Inference
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
Cc: Beth Carter <beth@pulsebio.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>, Raj Singh <raj@pulsebio.com>
Date: Fri, 20 Apr 2028 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Refit request — trimming features for pilot budget

Hannah — attaching a concise proposal PDF and three-line pricing table per your ask. Key assumptions (please confirm):
- Committed tokens per month: 250M (covers current short-gen volume + embeddings peak)
- Pilot Slim removes: realtime reranking, dedicated dispatch for tool-calls, long-context KV tier (keeps 4k KV instead of 32k)
- Per-token overage: $0.0009/token on Pilot Slim (vs $0.0016 on Full Stack)
- Re-enable credit: one-time credit equal to 50% of the monthly delta charged in month 1 if PulseBio signs a 6-month commitment (applied as account credit).

Downgrade/upgrade operational notes:
- Downgrade (Full -> Pilot Slim): seamless — we gate disabled features and lower concurrency limits. No data loss; only QoS limits. Effective immediately, pro-rate the invoice.
- Upgrade (Pilot Slim -> Full): we spin up the extra routing and capacity; canary traffic for 7 days. If enabling advanced rerank or tool-calls, we recommend a brief QA window (2–3 days). Re-enable cost = pro-rated difference plus any peak-capacity ramp charge (usually a one-time $2k engineering ramp for non-committed capacity).

I've included two attachments: redwood_proposal_v2.pdf (proposal + table) and a short appendix with the ramp charge logic.

Ben
Ben Carter
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference
attachments: redwood_proposal_v2.pdf

Cc: Raj Singh <raj@pulsebio.com>
Date: Tue, 25 Apr 2028 14:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Refit request — trimming features for pilot budget

Hi Ben/Hannah —

This is exactly the level of granularity Finance needed — thank you. A couple of follow-ups before I present on Monday:
1) Can you confirm the SLA (p95 latency) on Pilot Slim for short sequences (<=512 tokens)? We need to include that in the executive summary.
2) For the re-enable credit — can we cap the ramp charge if the re-enable happens within the first 90 days? Finance is sensitive to surprise one-off fees.

If you can reply by Friday EOD with those two items I can finalize the memo.

Thanks,
Beth
Beth Carter
Head of Product, PulseBio
